blindSummary:
The devolved administration publicly maintains an LGBTQ+ action plan with a standing update page issued after a supreme-court judgment (19 December 2025) on sex-based rights, and has enacted statutory school guidance (consultation May 2025) obliging schools to challenge bullying and harassment on gender-reassignment grounds with recording and monitoring, alongside dedicated guidance for supporting trans children in development through 2025–26. These measures represent an active institutional posture of inclusion at a time when the country-wide equality watchdog's single-sex-services code (in force 5 August 2026) creates a biological-sex facility-exclusion floor that applies here equally.

For a visitor the practical risk of service refusal is unchanged — the code binds facilities here as elsewhere — but the visible institutional commitment (action plan maintained, school recording obligations, publicly disclosed guidance work) shapes policing culture and public discourse. This state/province's published protection programmes differ from the national posture.
blindSourceSummaries: Regional administration's LGBTQ+ action-plan document for young people (posted January 2026): part of the standing devolved inclusion programme whose update page answers a supreme-court judgment of 19 December 2025 on sex-based rights.

Regional administration's statutory school guidance (consultation May 2025): obliges schools to challenge bullying and harassment on sex, gender-reassignment and sexual-orientation grounds, with incident recording/monitoring and a parental escalation route.
A public-policy institute rapid evidence review commissioned to inform the separate national guidance on schools supporting trans children and young people, developed through 2025-26.
Regional administration transparency release: publicly disclosed correspondence evidencing the trans-children school-guidance consultation work.
blindLocalsOnly: The school guidance, young-people action-plan material and recording duties bear on resident families and pupils; for a short-term visitor they register only as a protective institutional climate.
